text: Jamia Millia Islamia is a public research university located in Delhi, India. It was originally established in Aligarh, United Provinces (present-day Uttar Pradesh), during the British Raj on 29 October 1920, by nationalist leaders and students of Aligarh Muslim University, in response to their demand for a National Muslim University free from government influence, which they perceived as pro-British. The founding members included Mohammad Ali Jauhar, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Dr. Mukhtar Ahmad Ansari, and Abdul Majeed Khwaja, with the foundation stone laid by Mahmud Hasan Deobandi, an Islamic scholar and activist of the Indian independence movement, who was invited to Aligarh; his speech was read aloud by his student Shabbir Ahmad Usmani. The foundation committee included Kifayatullah Dehlawi, Hussain Ahmad Madani, Syed Sulaiman Nadwi, Abdul Haq, Abdul Bari Firangi Mahali, Shabbir Ahmad Usmani, Sanaullah Amritsari, Syed Mahmud, and Saifuddin Kitchlew. Jauhar served as the first vice-chancellor from 1920 to 1923, and Khan served as the first chancellor from 1920 to 1927. In 1925, the university moved from Aligarh to Karol Bagh, New Delhi, and on 1 March 1935, the foundation stone for a school building was laid at Okhla, then a nondescript village in the southern outskirts of Delhi. All institutions of Jamia Millia Islamia, except Jamia Press, the Maktaba, and the library, moved to the new campus in 1936. The University Grants Commission granted it deemed status in 1962, and it became a central university by an act of the Indian parliament passed on 26 December 1988. The university was founded by Mohammad Ali Jauhar, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Mahmud Hasan Deobandi, Mukhtar Ahmed Ansari, Abdul Majeed Khwaja, Zakir Hussain, Mahatma Gandhi, and Maulana Azad. Mahatma Gandhi supported the university, believing it could shape students through a shared culture and worldview, and he sent his youngest son Devdas Gandhi to teach Hindi at Jamia. In 2020, Jamia Millia Islamia was ranked 1st among all central universities in India by the Ministry of Education. In December 2021, it received an 'A++' ranking from the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC). On 26 May 2017, Najma Heptulla became the 11th and first woman Chancellor of the university; in April 2019, Najma Akhtar became the first woman Vice Chancellor, serving until 12 November 2023. On 13 March 2023, Mufaddal Saifuddin was elected the 12th Chancellor. In 2006, King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia visited the university and donated ₹130 crore (US$30 million) for a library and research center. In 2019, the university became a center of protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act, when Delhi Police used tear gas and entered the campus on 13 and 15 December 2019, leading to injuries and sparking protests at other universities. The campus spans a large area in Okhla, Delhi, and includes the Nawab Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi Sports Complex, which hosts cricket tournaments, Indian women's cricket matches, Ranji Trophy and Vijaya Trophy matches, Women's Cricket Test matches, Women's World Cup matches, Blind's Cricket World Cup matches, and served as a practice ground for the Commonwealth Games. The complex has facilities for cricket, football, lawn tennis, volleyball, badminton, basketball, jogging track, athletics, table tennis, yoga, snooker, hockey, and a gymnasium. The University Library System, with centralized and departmental libraries and archives, holds over 600,000 books, approximately 143,000 subject-specific books, Urdu collections, 5,000 rare books, and 2,230 rare manuscripts; it provides access to open access videos, e-resources, eBooks, e-journals, databases, MOOCs, with 100 workstations and 200 computers. The campus includes the Central Mosque, located opposite the central library on Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Marg, with a capacity of over 1,000 people. The university's governing structure includes the Amir-i-Jamia (chancellor), Shaikh-ul-Jamia (vice-chancellor), Naib Shaikh-ul-Jamia (Pro-Vice-Chancellor), and Musajjil (Registrar), with the President of India as Visitor. The Anjuman (University Court) is the supreme authority, overseeing the Majlis-i-Muntazimah (Executive Council), Majlis-i-Talimi (Academic Council), and Majlis-i-Maliyat (Finance Committee); the Executive Council is the highest executive body, and the Academic Council is responsible for maintaining educational standards. Jamia Millia Islamia has eleven faculties offering academic and extension programs. The Faculty of Law, established in 1989, offered only a three-year LL.B. until the early 2000s and began offering a five-year integrated B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) from 2002–2003; it also offers a two-year LLM in personal law, corporate law, and criminal law, a Ph.D., and an Executive LL.M. for professionals. It secured the 6th rank among law schools in India as per NIRF 2024. The Faculty of Engineering and Technology (FET), established in 1985, offers programs in PhD, M.Tech., M.Sc., B.Tech., and B.Sc. in Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics & Communication, Computer, Aeronautics, Applied Sciences & Humanities, and Environmental Science, with specializations in Artificial Intelligence, Data Sciences, VLSI Design, Environmental Science and Engineering, and others. In the Times Higher Education Subject Ranking-2024, JMI ranked 401–500 in Engineering and Technology, with a national rank of 11 among institutions and 2nd among universities; it ranked 501–600 in computer science, 16th among Indian institutions, and 7th among Indian universities. Jamia is the only central university with a Faculty of Architecture & Ekistics, established in 2001–2002, offering B.Arch and B.Des, M.Plan, M.Des, and PhD programs in Architecture, Planning, Design, and Ekistics, with departments for Architecture, Planning, and Design and Innovation. The Faculty of Humanities includes departments for Arabic, English, Hindi, History and Culture, Islamic Studies, Persian, Iranology, Urdu, Sanskrit, and Foreign Languages such as Korean, Japanese, Turkish, German, French, and Spanish & Latin American; the Sanskrit Department offers two certificate programs in Sanskrit and Yoga, and the Foreign Language Department offers certificate, diploma, and advanced diploma courses in Pashto, Persian, French, Italian, Spanish, Russian, Portuguese, Turkish, Chinese, Korean, and Uzbek. Islamic Studies, established as a separate department in 1988 under Zayn al-Abidin Sajjad Meerthi, publishes an annual magazine, Sada e Jauhar. The Faculty of Fine Arts has six departments offering BFA, MFA, diploma, and certificate courses in Painting, Sculpture, Applied Arts, Art Education, Graphic Art, Art History & Appreciation, Curatorial Practices, Art Management, and Conceptual Art Practice; it offers certificate programs in Design and Innovation, Textile Design, Creative Photography, Calligraphy, Art Appreciation & Art Writing, Art & Aesthetics, and Graphic Art (Print Making), and has an art gallery named after M. F. Hussain. The Faculty of Social Sciences consists of nine departments: Social Sciences, Psychology, Economics, Political Science, Sociology, Social Work, Adult Continuing Education and Extension, Commerce and Business Studies, and Library and Information Science, based at Gulistan-e-Ghalib and known as the Main Campus. The Faculty of Sciences includes Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Geography, and Computer Science, with associated centers: FTK-Centre for Information Technology, Centre for Theoretical Physics, and Centre for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology. The Faculty of Life Sciences, based in Srinivasa Ramanujan Block at Mujeeb Bagh Campus, includes Biosciences and Biotechnology, offering Ph.D., postgraduate, undergraduate, and diploma programs in Unani Pharmacy and Unani Medicine. The Teachers’ Training Institute, established in 1938 and later renamed Teachers’ College, offers B.Ed., M.Ed., M.A., and diploma, M.Phil., and doctoral programs in Education through its departments of Educational Studies and Institute of Advanced Studies in Education. The Faculty of Dentistry offers B.D.S. programs. The Faculty of Management Studies includes departments for Management Studies, Hospital Management & Hospice Studies, and Tourism & Hospitality Management. The Anwar Jamal Kidwai Mass Communication Research Centre, established in 1982, offers postgraduate courses in Mass Communication, Convergent Journalism, Development Communication, Visual Effect and Animation, and postgraduate diplomas in Still Photography and Visual Communication, Acting and Broadcast Technology. The FTK-Centre for Information Technology provides internet facilities for faculty, staff, research scholars, and students. The Centre for Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation Services offers B.P.T., M.P.T. (Sports, Orthopaedics, Neurology, Cardiopulmonary), and a Ph.D. The Centre for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology promotes research in nano-fabrication, nano-devices, nano-materials, nano-structures, nano-biotechnology, nano-medicine, and nano-structure characterization, offering PhD and M.Tech. (Nanotechnology) programs. The Centre for European and Latin American Studies offers part-time certificate, diploma, and advanced diploma courses in French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Russian, and M.Phil/Ph.D. in European and Latin American Studies. The MMAJ Academy of International Studies, formerly the Academy of Third World Studies, was established in 1988 under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and renamed after Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar; it offers M.Phil. and Ph.D. in International Studies, postgraduate courses in Politics: International and Area Studies, and language courses in Uzbek and Chinese, with a library and documentation centre named after Abid Husain. Other academic and non-academic centers include the Dr. Zakir Husain Institute of Islamic Studies, Centre for Distance and Open Learning, Nelson Mandela Centre for Peace and Conflict Resolution, Multidisciplinary Centre for Advance Research and Studies (MCARS), Centre for Theoretical Physics, FTK-Centre for Information Technology, Centre for Jawaharlal Nehru Studies, and Centre for Comparative Religions and Civilizations. In 2023, during the centenary convocation on 23 July, former Vice-Chancellor Najma Akhtar announced that the university has obtained central government approval to establish a medical college. Jamia won its first gold and silver medals in wrestling at the All India Inter University Championship in 1977. The university installed 2,250-kilowatt solar panels as part of a green campaign and remodeled its existing Gate No. 13 into the Centenary Gate, inaugurated on its 103rd foundation day. In 2024, Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Mazhar Asif was appointed as the Vice Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia.

The Academy of International Studies, formerly known as the Academy of Third World Studies, was established in 1988 under the initiative of then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi to conduct inter-disciplinary research on social, political, and economic issues related to developing countries. It was later renamed after Maulana Mohamad Ali Jauhar, one of the co-founders of Jamia Millia Islamia. The academy offers M.Phil and Ph.D. programmes in International Studies, postgraduate courses in Politics: International and Area Studies, and language courses in Uzbek and Chinese. It also maintains a library and documentation centre named after Abid Husain. Jamia Millia Islamia has a range of academic and non-academic centers, including the Dr. Zakir Husain Institute of Islamic Studies, Centre for Distance and Open Learning, Nelson Mandela Centre for Peace and Conflict Resolution, Multidisciplinary Centre for Advance Research and Studies (MCARS), Centre for Theoretical Physics, FTK-Centre for Information Technology, Centre for Jawaharlal Nehru Studies, Centre for Comparative Religions and Civilizations, Centre for West Asian Studies, Dr. K.R. Narayanan Centre for Dalit and Minorities Studies, Academy of Professional Development of Urdu Medium Teachers, Centre for North East Studies and Policy Research, India – Arab Cultural Centre, Centre for Culture Media & Governance, Centre for the Study of Social Exclusion and Inclusive Policy, UGC-Human Resource Development Centre, Centre for Coaching and Career Planning, Jamia's Premchand Archives & Literary Centre, Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra, Sarojini Naidu Centre for Women's Studies, University Counseling & Guidance Centre, Centre for Early Childhood Development and Research, and Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (CIE). The university provides education from nursery to senior secondary level. Internationally, Jamia Millia Islamia is ranked 851–900 in the QS World University Rankings 2025 and 206 in Asia in 2024; it is ranked 501–600 globally and 148 in Asia by the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2024, and 172 among emerging economies in 2022. In the Moscow-based Round University Ranking 2024, it is ranked 256 out of 1169 globally. According to U.S. News & World Report 2024–2025, it is ranked 718 in Best Global Universities, 205 in Asia, and 8 in India. In the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2024, Jamia Millia Islamia is ranked 13th overall in India, 6th in law, 7th in architecture, 8th in dental, 24th in engineering, 19th in research institutes, and 25th in management. It was also ranked third among universities in India by NIRF in 2024. The university organizes cultural festivals, including an annual festival and the Talimi Mela on its Foundation Day, 29 to 30 October each year. It also has a legacy of the national cultural festival MiRAAS, initiated by the Dean Students of Welfare, which featured cultural and competitive events but has not been organized since 2017. Since its inception, Jamia Millia Islamia has produced notable alumni such as Shah Rukh Khan, Kabir Khan, Mouni Roy, Arfa Khanum Sherwani, Barkha Dutt, Anjana Om Kashyap, Ampareen Lyngdoh, Kunwar Danish Ali, Tabish Mehdi, Virendar Sehwag, Imran Raza Ansari, Danish Siddiqui, and Mohammad Najeeb Qasmi.
